Langevin thermostat: canonical distributions, timestep bias and correlation Compare harmonic BAOAB with canonical and discrete-Lyapunov stationary distributions, and with continuous/discrete time correlations. Assumptions, units and boundaries Mass, Boltzmann constant, frequency, friction and temperature are one. Use 32768 replicas, burn time 20, steps 0.4/0.2/0.1 and correlation lag 2; require h*omega<2. Adopted numerical method Compose force B and drift A half steps with exact OU noise O in B-A-O-A-B order. Record covariance, three CDFs, energy mean/variance and position correlation. dq=p dt,dp=−ω2q dt−γp dt+2γT dWdq=pdt,dp=−ω2qdt−γpdt+2γT​dW Σ=MΣMT+Q,Σh=diag⁡(T/ω2,T(1−h2ω2/4))Σ=MΣMT+Q,Σh​=diag(T/ω2,T(1−h2ω2/4)) References and measured quantities Check against a SciPy discrete-Lyapunov solve and explicit harmonic covariance diag(T/omega²,T(1-h²omega²/4)). Separate second-order momentum bias from sampling error and evaluate burn transients from the map. A separate matrix exponential gives continuous correlation. Verification limits and failures Distribution checks use a harmonic potential and fixed seeds. Exact position variance does not remove finite-step momentum bias. Evidence does not transfer to other thermostats, general molecules or long ab initio MD. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded.
